import mir_eval

# Adjust intervals to ensure matching time spans before computing mutual information
adj_ref_intervals, adj_ref_labels = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(
    ref_intervals, ref_labels, t_min=0.0
)
adj_est_intervals, adj_est_labels = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(
    est_intervals, est_labels, t_min=0.0, t_max=adj_ref_intervals.max()
)

# Compute mutual information metrics between reference and estimate
mi, ami, nmi = mir_eval.segment.mutual_information(
    adj_ref_intervals, adj_ref_labels, adj_est_intervals, adj_est_labels
)

# Compute mutual information of the reference with itself as a strong oracle
self_mi, self_ami, self_nmi = mir_eval.segment.mutual_information(
    adj_ref_intervals, adj_ref_labels, adj_ref_intervals, adj_ref_labels
)

# Normalized Mutual Information is bounded in [0, 1], and identical segmentations yield 1.0
assert 0.0 <= nmi <= 1.0 + 1e-6, f"NMI should be in [0, 1], got {nmi}"
assert abs(self_nmi - 1.0) < 1e-6, f"NMI of a segmentation with itself must be 1.0, got {self_nmi}"

print(f"__CHECK__ mutual_information {mi:.4f}, {ami:.4f}, {nmi:.4f}")
